On a read, `Segment.get` calls `recordRead(entry, now)` (`guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java:2542-2547`), which appends the entry to the segment's lock-free `recencyQueue` (a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`, field at line 2548) — no segment lock needed since the queue itself is concurrent. That queue is later drained, under the segment lock (`@GuardedBy("this")`), by `drainRecencyQueue()` (lines 2590-2602), which polls entries off it and reorders them in the real LRU `accessQueue`. `drainRecencyQueue` is invoked from lock-holding paths like `Segment.postReadCleanup`/`runLockedCleanup` on subsequent writes/reads that do acquire the lock.

ANSWER: A read calls `Segment.recordRead(entry, now)`, which just does `recencyQueue.add(entry)` on the lock-free `recencyQueue` (a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`) — no segment lock is taken. That queue is later drained, while holding the segment lock, by `Segment.drainRecencyQueue()`, which polls each entry and moves it to the end of the real LRU `accessQueue`.
